data.name: Ata
data.gender_notes: Ata is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ata is a beautiful and concise Arabic name meaning 'gift' or 'blessing'. It reflects generosity, divine favor, and a kind-hearted personality. Frequently used in compound names like Ata-ur-Rehman. The name Ata carries the meaning “Gift, Blessing, Giving” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Arabic. Parents who choose Ata usually hope their child will grow to embody gift, blessing, giving and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes a person considered a divine gift — someone who brings value, light, and joy to the lives of others.
data.etymology: Ata belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift, Blessing, Giving.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ata total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_english.name: Ata
in_english.meaning: obedience, obedience act, obedience order, obedient
in_english.long_meaning: Ata is an Arabic name that means obedience, obedience act, obedience order, obedient. It is derived from the Arabic root طَعَنَ (ta`na), which means to obey, to follow. In Islamic tradition, Ata is considered a virtuous name that signifies a person who is obedient to Allah and follows His commands. In Arabic, the word اطاع (ataa) means to obey, and it is used in the Quran to describe those who obey Allah. In Urdu, the name Ata is written اطاع and means obedience. In Hindi, it is written आता and also means obedience. In Pashto, it is written اتا and means obedience. In Turkish, it is written Ata and means obedience. In English, it is written Ata and means obedience, obedience act, obedience order, obedient.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ata carries a profound cultural significance in the Islamic community as it embodies the concept of Khudrat (divine favor), a central belief in Islam. On a societal level, this name also implies the superior value placed on hospitality and generosity, as gifts are exchanged frequently in various Islamic cultures as signs of goodwill, respect, and friendship.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, choosing the name Ata as a personal identifier can be seen as a symbolic reflection of one's deep connection to Allah, as every blessing, talent, or possession a believer holds is deemed a gift from the Almighty. It can serve as a reminder of their dependence on God, encouraging a life of gratitude and humility.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Ata means "given" or "bestowed" in Arabic. It symbolizes the idea that everything comes from Allah, and we are merely the recipients of His blessings. Our names, our lives, and all our accomplishments are all gifts from Allah.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ata ibn Rabah Al-Qurashi was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad. The name Ata carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ata ibn Rabah Al-Qurashi was a prominent Sahabi (companion) of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and a narrator of Hadith. He was born in Mecca and was a member of the Quraysh tribe.
